# Project Guidelines

## Git — this is a fork, upstream is read-only

`origin` is **https://github.com/ussdeveloper/osiris** (our fork) and is the only
remote we ever write to. `upstream` is **https://github.com/simplifaisoul/osiris**
(the original project) and is **reference only**.

Hard rules:

- **Never push to `upstream`.** No `git push upstream`, no `git remote set-url`, no
  restoring `origin` to the upstream URL.
- **Never open pull requests against `simplifaisoul/osiris`.** No
  `gh pr create --repo simplifaisoul/osiris`.
- Do all work on a local branch of the fork, then push to `origin`.
- Fetching from `upstream` for reference is fine; never merge it in — not even
  incidental `git pull`, which resolves to the tracked upstream on a shared clone.

`AGENTS.md` at the repo root is generated by `next dev` and gitignored — do not put
durable instructions there. This file is the source of truth for project directives.

## Stack notes

Next.js 16 (Turbopack, App Router) + TypeScript. Before writing framework code, read
`node_modules/next/dist/docs/` — the version in use has breaking changes against
older conventions.

## Build and test

```bash
npm run dev     # http://localhost:3000
npm run build
npm test        # vitest run
npm run lint    # eslint
```

`npm test` has one known pre-existing failure: `src/lib/geo.test.ts` expects
`4,200 km` while the runner's locale formats `4200 km`. Unrelated to feature work.

## CCTV camera catalogue

Region sources live in `src/app/api/cctv/` and are registered in `route.ts`
(`RAW_REGION_FETCHERS`). Large catalogues are generated, not typed by hand — keep the
scraper in `scratch/` next to the generated module and commit the raw harvest
alongside it, so output stays reproducible.

The catalogue is cached twice, so a new source does **not** appear until both layers
are cleared: 30-minute in-memory cache (`src/lib/sourceCache.ts`) and
`.cache/cctv-catalog.json`. Delete the snapshot file and restart the dev server.
